title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is part of the proof of a 'geometric finiteness' corollary (Corollaire 1, previous page). Setting: X and Y are reduced schemes of finite type over an algebraically closed field k. f, g : X -> Y are morphisms with pi_1(f) = pi_1(g) as outer homomorphisms.
- Part a): if Y embeds via i : Y -> G into a commutative algebraic group G that is an extension of an abelian variety by a torus (a semi-abelian variety), then i∘g = tau_a ∘ i∘f for a unique a.
- Part b): if Y is an 'elementary Artin variety' (a successive fibration in curves, i.e. a good/Artin neighbourhood), X is irreducible and f or g is dominant, then f = g.
- The previous page notes that for a) it suffices to assume H_1(f, Z_l) = H_1(g, Z_l) for one prime l different from the characteristic.

This page finishes the proof of a). Fix an origin o in X(k) and reduce to f(o) = g(o) = 0. Then f = g must be shown, and it is enough to look at the induced maps on abelianised l-adic fundamental groups. Take the generalized Albanese variety J of X, of type 'extension of an AV by a torus' (Serre's generalized Albanese). Three facts are used:
1) Universal property: every f : X -> G with f(o) = 0 factors uniquely as X --can--> J --phi--> G, with phi a homomorphism of algebraic groups.
2) A homomorphism of semi-abelian varieties is determined by its action on Tate modules H_1( , Z_l), because the l-power torsion points are Zariski dense.
3) H_1(X, Z_l) ≅ H_1(J, Z_l).
Write f = phi∘can and g = psi∘can. By 3), H_1(f) = H_1(g) gives H_1(phi) = H_1(psi). By 2), phi = psi, hence f = g. A cross-reference '(p. 30)' presumably points to where 3) is proved.

Remark a): one cannot conclude f = g in general. Take X = Y = G: translations induce the identity on pi_1(G), at least in characteristic 0 or when G is an abelian variety, without being the identity. The caveat correctly reflects that in characteristic p translations can act nontrivially on the wild part of pi_1 of tori or additive groups.

Remark b) starts the anabelian case: equality f = g will be proved under the anabelian hypothesis plus dominance. The next page gives constant maps as the counterexample without dominance. Its strategy is to embed the Artin elementary variety in a semi-abelian G, so that i∘g = tau_u∘i∘f, and then analyse pi_1 of an open set V with V + u contained in Y.

Purpose: this is the 'injectivity / finiteness' half of a Hom-form anabelian statement over an algebraically closed field. Dominant morphisms into elementary anabelian varieties are determined by their action on pi_1, and morphisms into semi-abelian targets are determined up to translation by their action on pi_1^ab.
errors: Fact 3) 'H_1(X,Z_l) ≅ H_1(J,Z_l)' is overstated. For non-normal or singular X (e.g. a nodal cubic: H_1 = Z_l but the Albanese for morphisms is trivial) it fails. Even for smooth X, H_1(X,Z_l) can have torsion (e.g. an Enriques surface) that J does not see.

What the argument actually needs is that the image of H_1(X,Z_l) -> T_l(J) has finite index (equivalently it spans T_l(J) ⊗ Q_l). That suffices because T_l(J) is torsion-free. So the proof survives, but the claimed isomorphism is not correct as stated for 'reduced schemes of finite type'.
X should be assumed connected (implicit in choosing a single origin o and in the outer homomorphism formulation).
The labels of the sub-remarks are slightly inconsistent: the remark labelled 'a)' refers to 'l'hyp. dans c)', which presumably means the hypothesis of part a).

ideas.what: Morphisms from X to a semi-abelian variety are, after fixing a base point, homomorphisms from the generalized (semi-abelian) Albanese of X.
ideas.modern_name: Serre's generalized Albanese variety / universal property of Alb for morphisms to semi-abelian varieties
ideas.where_published: Standard; used implicitly in SGA/FGA-era work, but not as here

ideas.what: A homomorphism of semi-abelian varieties is determined by its action on l-adic Tate modules because the l-power torsion is dense.
ideas.modern_name: Injectivity of Hom(G,G') -> Hom(T_l G, T_l G')

ideas.what: Maps of X into a semi-abelian variety are determined up to translation by their action on pi_1^ab ⊗ Z_l (single l prime to p).
ideas.modern_name: Rigidity of maps to semi-abelian varieties via l-adic homology / Albanese
ideas.where_published: Part of the 'Longue Marche' manuscript (1981), circulated in transcription

ideas.what: Translations act trivially on pi_1(G) only in char 0 or for abelian varieties; implicit awareness that in char p translations on tori/G_a act nontrivially on wild covers.
ideas.modern_name: Non-homotopy-invariance of translations in étale pi_1 in char p (Artin–Schreier phenomena)

ideas.what: Dominant morphisms into an elementary Artin variety (iterated fibration in hyperbolic curves) are determined by pi_1; dominance is necessary (constant maps).
ideas.modern_name: Injectivity part of the Hom-anabelian conjecture over algebraically closed fields; homotopy rigidity of maps to hyperbolic targets
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Letter to Faltings 1983; Esquisse 1984) for the anabelian framework; classical over C via hyperbolic geometry
ideas.where_published: Lettre à Faltings (1983), Esquisse d'un programme (1984) mention elementary anabelian varieties; this specific geometric-finiteness corollary appears in La Longue Marche (1981)

missed.claim: An explicit 'geometric finiteness' corollary: over any algebraically closed field (including char p, with l ≠ p), dominant maps X -> Y into an elementary Artin variety are determined by pi_1, and maps into semi-abelian targets by H_1(-,Z_l) up to translation. The proof is via the generalized Albanese and an open-set translation argument. This is a minor but explicit early formulation of the injectivity half of the geometric Hom-conjecture; it is largely folklore and close to known rigidity statements.
missed.quote: on conclut (p. 30) que H_1(f) = H_1(g) implique ... H_1(φ) = H_1(ψ), donc par 2°) que φ = ψ, donc f = g
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Documents the precise form of the 'finitude géométrique' Grothendieck had in mind in 1981, including char p and the dominance hypothesis; mostly of historical interest.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is a standard Albanese/Tate-module rigidity argument, applied to an early formulation of the geometric injectivity in anabelian geometry. Interesting historically (char p caveat, the role of dominance) but not new to specialists.
